etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin convenientia, from conveniens (“suitable”), present participle of convenire (“to come together, suit”). Doublet of convenance.

quote.citation: c. 1599–1602 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Hamlet, Prince of Denmarke”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene vii]:
quote.text: Let's further think of this; / Weigh what convenience both of time and means / May fit us to our shape.

quote.citation: 1782–1785, William Cowper, “(please specify the page)”, in The Task, a Poem, […], London:  […]  J[oseph] Johnson;  […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Thus first Necessity invented stools, / Convenience next suggested elbow-chairs […]

definitions.definition: Any object that makes life more convenient; a helpful item.

quote.citation: 1726 October 28, [Jonathan Swift], Travels into Several Remote Nations of the World.  […]  [Gulliver’s Travels], volume I, London:  […]  Benj[amin] Motte, […], →OCLC, part I (A Voyage to Lilliput):
quote.text: A pair of spectacles […]  and several other little conveniences.

quote.citation: 1838 (date written), L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter XVII, in Lady Anne Granard; or, Keeping up Appearances. […], volume I, London: Henry Colburn, […], published 1842, →OCLC, page 223:
quote.text: ...let Fanchette come in a hackney-coach in the morning, and I will direct the housekeeper to send you something of every thing—plate, candlesticks, lamps, damask—and you won't take it amiss if we should happen to have game or poultry come up that I put that amongst the conveniences;...

quote.citation: 1977, David Byrne (lyrics and music), “Don't Worry About the Government”, in Talking Heads: 77, performed by Talking Heads:
quote.text: It's over there, it's over there / My building has every convenience / It's gonna make life easy for me

definitions.definition: (chiefly British) Ellipsis of public convenience: a public lavatory.
